source_refs.note: Book p. 99-101: 6.5.2 Properties of G.P. (i)-(vi), Examples 12-16 (Ex 14 Step 1/Step 2); Exercise 6.5 not included

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum G.P. ki chhe khasoosiyat (properties) dekhenge. Yeh properties sawal hal karte waqt shortcut ka kaam deti hain, khaas tor par jab saabit karna ho ke koi numbers G.P. mein hain. Har property ke saath hum aik chhoti misaal bhi lenge, taa ke ratta na lagana pare. Aik baat pehle se zehan mein rakh lijiye: in sab properties ko parakhne ka aik hi tareeqa hai. Nayi sequence ki do lagataar terms ka ratio nikaalo; agar woh constant (har jagah aik jaisa) nikle to nayi sequence bhi G.P. hai. Isi aik idea se aap har property khud saabit kar sakte hain.

(i) Agar G.P. ki har term ko aik hi non-zero number se zarb ya taqseem (divide) kiya jaye to nayi sequence bhi G.P. hoti hai. Yani agar \(g_1, g_2, g_3, \ldots, g_n, \ldots\) G.P. mein hain aur \(k\) koi non-zero number hai, to

items: (a) \(kg_1, kg_2, kg_3, \ldots, kg_n, \ldots\) G.P. mein hain.

blocks.text: (ii) G.P. ki terms ke reciprocals (ulte, yani \(\frac{1}{\text{term}}\)) bhi G.P. banate hain. Yani agar \(a, b, c\) G.P. mein hain to \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}\) bhi G.P. mein hain.
(iii) Agar G.P. ki har term ko aik hi power di jaye to naye numbers bhi G.P. banate hain. Yani agar \(a, b, c\) G.P. mein hain to \(a^{n}, b^{n}, c^{n}\) bhi G.P. mein hain.
(iv) Teen numbers \(a, b, c\) G.P. mein tab aur sirf tab (if and only if) hain jab \(b^{2} = ac\). Yeh sab se zyada istemal hone wali property hai.
(v) Agar positive numbers \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n, \ldots\) G.P. mein hon to \(\log a_1, \log a_2, \log a_3, \ldots, \log a_n, \ldots\) A.P. mein hote hain, aur ulta bhi sach hai (vice-versa).

(vi) Do G.Ps. ko term by term zarb ya taqseem karne se bhi G.P. banti hai. Yani agar \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n\) aur \(b_1, b_2, b_3, \ldots, b_n\) G.P. mein hon to \(a_1b_1, a_2b_2, a_3b_3, \ldots\) aur \(\frac{a_1}{b_1}, \frac{a_2}{b_2}, \frac{a_3}{b_3}, \ldots\) bhi G.P. mein hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab har property ko aik hi G.P. \(2, 6, 18\) (\(r = 3\)) par aazma kar dekhte hain:
(i) 5 se zarb: \(10, 30, 90\), ratio phir bhi 3. 2 se taqseem: \(1, 3, 9\), ratio phir bhi 3.
(ii) Reciprocals: \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{18}\); har term pichli ka \(\frac{1}{3}\), yani \(r = \frac{1}{3}\).
(iii) Squares: \(4, 36, 324\); ratio 9, yani \(3^{2}\).
(iv) \(6^{2} = 36\) aur \(2 \times 18 = 36\). Barabar!
(v) \(\log 2, \log 6, \log 18\): har agla pichle se \(\log 3\) zyada (kyun ke \(\log 6 = \log 2 + \log 3\)), yani A.P. jis ka \(d = \log 3\).
(vi) Doosri G.P. \(1, 2, 4\) lein. Zarb: \(2, 12, 72\) (ratio 6 = \(3 \times 2\)). Taqseem: \(2, 3, \frac{9}{2}\) (ratio \(\frac{3}{2}\)).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh properties sach kyun hain? Har case mein nayi sequence ki do lagataar terms ka ratio nikaal kar dekhiye:
(i) \(\frac{kg_n}{kg_{n-1}} = r\): \(k\) upar neeche cancel ho gaya, ratio wahi raha.
(ii) \(\frac{1/b}{1/a} = \frac{a}{b} = \frac{1}{r}\): naya ratio \(\frac{1}{r}\) hai, jo bhi constant hai.
(iii) \(\frac{b^{n}}{a^{n}} = \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^{n} = r^{n}\): yeh bhi constant.
(iv) G.P. ka matlab hai \(\frac{b}{a} = \frac{c}{b}\) (dono ratios barabar). Cross-multiply karein to \(b^{2} = ac\). Dhyan dein: yahan \(a, b, c\) non-zero hone chahiye. \(0, 0, 5\) mein \(b^{2} = 0 = ac\) hai magar yeh G.P. nahin.
(v) \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) ka log lein: \(\log a_n = \log a_1 + (n-1)\log r\). Yeh bilkul A.P. ki general term ki shakal hai, jis mein \(d = \log r\). Numbers positive is liye chahiye ke log sirf positive numbers ka hota hai.
(vi) Ratios aapas mein zarb ho jate hain: \(\frac{a_nb_n}{a_{n-1}b_{n-1}} = r_1r_2\), aur taqseem mein \(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\).
Ab kitab ki misaalein. In sab mein aik hi hathyaar hai: general term \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\). Farq sirf yeh hai ke kis sawal mein kaun si cheez maloom hai aur kaun si dhoondni hai.

blocks.title: Example 12
blocks.problem: Find the eighth term of a geometric sequence for which \(a_1 = -3\) and \(r = -2\).
steps:
Given: \(a_1 = -3\), \(r = -2\), \(n = 8\).
To find: \(a_8\).
Method: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke formula \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) ki chaar cheezon mein se teen (\(a_1, r, n\)) maloom hain. To seedha values rakh denge. Bas negative signs ka khayal rakhna hai.

Step 1: General term mein values rakhein
\[a_n = a_1 \cdot r^{n-1}\]
\[a_8 = (-3) \cdot (-2)^{8-1}\]
Kyun: aathvin term ke liye \(r\) se \(8 - 1 = 7\) dafa zarb hota hai. \(-2\) ko bracket mein rakha, warna power ka sign gum ho jata.

Step 2: Power hal karein
\[a_8 = (-3) \cdot (-128)\]
Kyun: \(2^{7} = 128\), aur negative number ki odd (taaq) power negative hoti hai, is liye \((-2)^{7} = -128\).
Dhyan dein: yahan sign ki ghalti sab se aam hai.

Step 3: Zarb dein
\[a_8 = 384\]
Kyun: minus \(\times\) minus = plus, aur \(3 \times 128 = 384\).

Tasdeeq:
Terms likh kar dekhte hain, har dafa \(-2\) se zarb: \(-3, 6, -12, 24, -48, 96, -192, 384\). Aathvin term 384 hi hai. Sign bhi baari baari badal raha hai, jaisa negative \(r\) mein hona chahiye.

blocks.title: Example 13
blocks.problem: Write an equation for the \(n\)th term of the geometric sequence \(3, 12, 48, 192, \ldots\)
steps:
Given: G.P. \(3, 12, 48, 192, \ldots\)
To find: \(a_n\) ka formula (equation).
Method: yahan koi khaas term nahin maangi gayi, balke aisa formula maanga gaya hai jo har term de. To \(a_1\) aur \(r\) nikaal kar \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) mein rakhenge aur \(n\) ko letter hi rehne denge.

Step 1: \(a_1\) aur \(r\) pehchaanein
\[a_1 = 3,\quad r = \dfrac{12}{3} = 4\]
Kyun: \(r\) = koi term \(\div\) pichli term. Tasalli ke liye: \(\frac{48}{12} = 4\) aur \(\frac{192}{48} = 4\). Sab barabar, to waqai G.P. hai.

Step 2: General term likhein
\[a_n = a_1 \cdot r^{n-1}\]
\[a_n = 3 \cdot 4^{n-1}\]
Kyun: sawal equation maang raha hai, is liye \(n\) variable hi rehta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(3 \cdot 4^{n-1}\) ko \(12^{n-1}\) mat banaiye; power sirf 4 par hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(n = 1, 2, 3, 4\) rakhein: \(3 \cdot 4^{0} = 3\), \(3 \cdot 4 = 12\), \(3 \cdot 16 = 48\), \(3 \cdot 64 = 192\). Di hui saari terms wapas mil gayin.

blocks.title: Example 14
blocks.problem: Find the tenth term of a geometric sequence for which \(a_4 = 108\) and \(r = 3\).
steps:
Given: \(a_4 = 108\), \(r = 3\).
To find: \(a_{10}\).
Method: masla yeh hai ke \(a_1\) nahin diya. Is liye kitab do qadam leti hai: Step 1 mein \(n = 4\) wali maloom term se \(a_1\) nikaalo, Step 2 mein usi formula se \(a_{10}\).

Step 1: \(a_1\) ki value nikaalein
Yahan \(n = 4\), \(r = 3\), \(a_4 = 108\).
\[a_n = a_1 \cdot r^{n-1}\]
\[a_4 = a_1 \cdot 3^{4-1}\]
\[108 = 27a_1\]
\[4 = a_1\]
Kyun: \(3^{3} = 27\); phir dono taraf 27 se divide karein: \(108 \div 27 = 4\).

Tasdeeq:
Aik shortcut se check karte hain: \(a_4\) se \(a_{10}\) tak \(r\) se chhe dafa zarb hota hai (10 \(-\) 4 = 6). To \(a_{10} = a_4 \cdot r^{6} = 108 \cdot 729 = 78732\). Wahi jawab! Yeh shortcut aap exam mein bhi istemal kar sakte hain.

blocks.title: Example 15
blocks.problem: Find the \(5^{\text{th}}\) term of the G.P., \(3, 6, 12, \ldots\)
steps:
Given: G.P. \(3, 6, 12, \ldots\)
To find: \(a_5\).
Method: pehle di hui terms se \(r\) nikaalenge, phir \(n = 5\) rakh kar general term lagayenge.

Step 1: \(r\) nikaalein
Yahan \(a_1 = 3\), \(a_2 = 6\), \(a_3 = 12\), is liye
\[r = \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2\]
Kyun: kisi term ko pichli term se divide karne se \(r\) milta hai; \(\frac{12}{6} = 2\) bhi yahi kehta hai.

Tasdeeq:
Double karte jayein: \(3, 6, 12, 24, 48\). Paanchvin term 48 hai.

blocks.title: Example 16
steps:
Given: \(a_4 = \frac{8}{27}\), \(a_7 = -\frac{64}{729}\).
To find: \(a_n\), yani general term.
Method: \(a_n\) likhne ke liye do cheezein chahiye: \(a_1\) aur \(r\). Dono di hui terms ko formula \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) ...(i) se likhenge. Phir aik ko doosri se divide karenge; is se \(a_1\) cancel ho jayega aur sirf \(r\) bachega. Yeh do terms wale sawalon ka pakka tareeqa hai.

Step 1: Di hui terms likhein
\[a_4 = a_1 r^{4-1} = a_1 r^{3}\]
\[a_1 r^{3} = \dfrac{8}{27} \quad \text{(ii)}\]
\[a_7 = a_1 r^{7-1} = a_1 r^{6}\]
\[a_1 r^{6} = \dfrac{-64}{729} \quad \text{(iii)}\]
Kyun: har di hui term do unknowns (\(a_1\) aur \(r\)) wali aik equation ban jati hai. Do equations, do unknowns: hal ho sakta hai.

Step 2: (iii) ko (ii) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{a_7}{a_4} = \dfrac{a_1 r^{6}}{a_1 r^{3}} = r^{3}\]
\[r^{3} = \dfrac{-64/729}{8/27} = \dfrac{-8}{27}\]
\[r^{3} = \left(\dfrac{-2}{3}\right)^{3}\]
\[\Rightarrow r = -\dfrac{2}{3}\]
Kyun: divide karne se \(a_1\) cancel ho gaya aur powers ka farq \(6 - 3 = 3\) bacha. Fraction ko fraction se divide karne ke liye ulta kar ke zarb: \(\frac{64}{729} \times \frac{27}{8} = \frac{8}{27}\). Hum sirf real value lete hain (\(-\frac{8}{27}\) ke baaqi do cube roots complex numbers hain).
Dhyan dein: negative number ka cube root negative hota hai, is liye \(r = -\frac{2}{3}\), \(+\frac{2}{3}\) nahin.

Step 3: \(a_1\) nikaalein
\(r^{3} = -\frac{8}{27}\) ko (ii) mein rakhein:
\[a_1\left(-\dfrac{8}{27}\right) = \dfrac{8}{27}\]
\[\Rightarrow a_1 = -1\]
Kyun: (ii) mein \(r^{3}\) hi aata hai jo humein pehle se maloom hai, is liye dobara cube karne ki zaroorat nahin. Dono taraf \(-\frac{8}{27}\) se divide karein to \(a_1 = -1\).

Step 4: \(a_n\) likhein
\(a_1 = -1\) aur \(r = \frac{-2}{3}\) ko (i) mein rakhne se:
\[a_n = (-1)\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[= (-1)(-1)^{n-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[= (-1)^{n}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
jab \(n \ge 1\).
Kyun: \(-\frac{2}{3} = (-1) \times \frac{2}{3}\), is liye power dono hisson par alag alag lagti hai. Phir \((-1)\) aur \((-1)^{n-1}\) ki powers jama hoti hain: \(1 + (n - 1) = n\).

Tasdeeq:
\(n = 4\): \((-1)^{4}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3} = \frac{8}{27}\). Sahi. \(n = 7\): \((-1)^{7}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{6} = -\frac{64}{729}\). Yeh bhi sahi. Dono di hui terms wapas mil gayin, is liye formula durust hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari taraf se practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin. Kisi G.P. mein \(a_3 = 12\) aur \(a_6 = 96\) hai. \(a_1\) aur \(r\) nikaaliye.
Example 16 wala tareeqa: \(\frac{a_6}{a_3} = \frac{a_1 r^{5}}{a_1 r^{2}} = r^{3} = \frac{96}{12} = 8\), to \(r = 2\).
Phir \(a_1 r^{2} = 12 \Rightarrow 4a_1 = 12 \Rightarrow a_1 = 3\). G.P.: \(3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96\). Tasdeeq ho gayi.
Khud sochiye: kya \(4, 10, 25\) G.P. mein hain? Property (iv) lagaiye: \(10^{2} = 100\) aur \(4 \times 25 = 100\). Haan!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. G.P. ki har term ko aik hi non-zero number se zarb ya taqseem karo to G.P. hi rehti hai (\(r\) wahi).
2. Reciprocals ki G.P. ka ratio \(\frac{1}{r}\); powers ki G.P. ka ratio \(r^{n}\).
3. Non-zero \(a, b, c\) G.P. mein hain sirf jab \(b^{2} = ac\).
4. Positive numbers ki G.P. ke logs A.P. banate hain (\(d = \log r\)).
5. Do G.Ps. ka term by term zarb ya taqseem bhi G.P. hai.
6. Do terms di hon to aik ko doosri se divide karo: \(a_1\) cancel, \(r\) ki power bachti hai.
7. Negative \(r\) ki odd power negative, even power positive.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \((-2)^{7} = 128\) likh dena: negative number ki odd power negative hoti hai, yani \(-128\).
2. Example 16 mein \(r = \frac{2}{3}\) le lena: negative number ka cube root negative hota hai.
3. Zero wali terms par \(b^{2} = ac\) lagana: G.P. ki koi term zero nahin hoti.
4. Yeh samajhna ke har term mein aik hi number jorne se bhi G.P. rehti hai: \(2, 6, 18\) mein 1 jorein to \(3, 7, 19\) bante hain, jo G.P. nahin. Sirf zarb ya taqseem chalti hai.
5. \(a_1\) diya na ho to seedha \(a_{10}\) ke formule mein ghalat \(a_1\) rakh dena: pehle maloom term se \(a_1\) nikaaliye (Example 14).
